strategy.summary: GET /orders/:id got slower when commit 62d8c6f ("Show each line's product name on an order") was added. In src/app.js:33 that commit calls findProduct() once for each line, one after another. Every store query is a simulated round trip of 6–9 ms (src/store.js), and an order has 8 lines, so the page now makes 10 sequential queries where it used to make 2: findOrder + orderLines ≈ 15–18 ms before, ≈ 75–90 ms now. That matches the reported change from about 22 to 88 ms p95. The plan is to guard the detail scenario in perf/orders.js with a scenario-scoped k6 threshold that fails while the page stays this slow, and to record the N+1 query as a defect for the API team. The application is not changed.
inScope: perf/orders.js: thresholds scoped to the detail scenario (p95, p99, error rate)
Request name tag on the detail request so /orders/:id is aggregated as one URL
Defect record of the N+1 product lookup
outOfScope: Changing src/ (the fix belongs to the API team, per the ticket)
perf/search.js and the list scenario's limits (the ticket says both are fine)
assumptions: Q1: the reviewer left the limits to me. The detail scenario gets p(95)<40 and p(99)<50 (ms). Healthy is about 22/25 ms, so that leaves room for CI noise, and it fails at today's 88/92 ms.
The app runs for real from `npm start` on BASE_URL (default http://localhost:4310), as .testforge.yml configures. Nothing is faked.

I can't read git history in this environment. The culprit commit is identified from its message (62d8c6f) and from the code it describes: the per-line findProduct loop in src/app.js:33, while orderLines already returns each line in one query (src/store.js:46).

TestForge's counted runs use smoke mode with --no-thresholds, so they prove the script runs and its checks pass. They do not prove the threshold breaches. That will be shown with a full `k6 run perf/orders.js` through run_command if the app is reachable.
openQuestions: Should the generic http_req_duration p(95)<2000 stay as a global ceiling? I plan to keep it unchanged.

cases.title: names the product on every line

defects.title: GET /orders/:id makes one sequential product query per line (N+1), about 4× slower
defects.description: AC1/AC3: commit 62d8c6f ("Show each line's product name on an order") added `for (const line of items) line.productName = (await findProduct(line.productId)).name;` at src/app.js:33. Every store call is a round trip of 6–9 ms (src/store.js ROUND_TRIP_MS + JITTER_MS), and every order has 8 lines. The order page used to make 2 queries (findOrder, orderLines) and now makes 10, one after another: about 15–18 ms before, about 75–90 ms now. That matches the reported change from 22/25 to 88/92 ms p95/p99. Expected: the product names come back in the existing orderLines query, or in one batched lookup. The detail scenario in perf/orders.js now has thresholds p(95)<40 and p(99)<50, which fail while this stays. k6 has no expected-to-fail mechanism, and TestForge's smoke runs use --no-thresholds, so the script itself passes in smoke mode.
defects.evidence: Smoke run of perf/orders.js: GET /orders took 12 ms and GET /orders/:id took 84.98 ms in the same iteration. The code path is src/app.js:33, with 8 awaited findProduct round trips per request.

review.standard: k6: Relying on checks for pass/fail — a test with passing checks but no thresholds always exits 0 (test-k6 anti-patterns); General: assert meaningful outcomes
review.summary: The new 'names the product on every line' check has no threshold behind it (no `checks` / `checks{scenario:detail}` entry in options.thresholds), so a full `k6 run perf/orders.js` exits 0 even when the check fails on every request.
review.failureScenario: The API team 'fixes' PERF-12 by dropping the per-line findProduct loop at src/app.js:33 (reverting 62d8c6f) instead of batching it. GET /orders/:id goes back to 2 round trips (~22 ms p95), returns 200 with no productName on any line. Then http_req_duration{scenario:detail} and http_req_failed{scenario:detail} both pass, the check fails 100% of the time, and k6 still exits 0. The guard passes while the order page has lost the behaviour that TC1's steps say this check protects. Adding e.g. `'checks{scenario:detail}': ['rate==1']` (or `checks: ['rate>0.99']`) next to lines 28–29 would make the check's failure fail the run.

Give any new perf script with exec-only scenarios one too.
